items.title: Civil Service Jobs: your account, searches and alerts
items.source: Civil Service Jobs website; GOV.UK, Working for the Civil Service
items.body: Most Civil Service vacancies are advertised on the Civil Service Jobs website. Create an account and fill in your profile once, so each application starts with your details already in place. Use the search to filter by location, grade, department, working pattern and salary. Then save your searches and switch on job alerts, so the site tells you when a matching role appears. Every advert has a closing date and time. Late applications are not accepted, so aim to submit well before the deadline. Websites can be busy in the last hours and a connection or login problem on the final evening can cost you the application. Keep a simple record of each role you apply for: the reference, the closing date, what you submitted and what stage it has reached.

questions.prompt: Where are most Civil Service vacancies advertised?

options.text: On the Civil Service Jobs website
Only in national newspapers
Only on department noticeboards
Only through recruitment agencies

questions.prompt: Why is it useful to save a search and turn on job alerts?

options.text: It guarantees an interview
You are told when a matching job is advertised, so you do not miss the closing date
It lets you apply after the closing date
It makes your application score higher

questions.prompt: A job closes at 11:55pm on Friday. When is the best time to submit your application?

options.text: At 11:50pm on Friday, so it is as fresh as possible
On Saturday, because the system usually allows a day's grace
Well before the deadline, for example by Wednesday
Never before Friday, in case you change your mind

questions.prompt: You have eight hours a week for job hunting. Describe a weekly routine that helps you stay on top of vacancies and applications.
questions.answer: A sensible routine: one session to check alerts and new vacancies and save the ones that fit; one session to read the advert and criteria of the best match and note which examples you will use; one or two sessions to write and edit the application ahead of the closing date; and a short session to update a tracking list (reference, closing date, stage) and practise tests or interview answers. Plan backwards from each closing date and leave time to proof-read and submit early.
questions.rubric: Should split time between searching, reading the advert, writing, tracking and practice, plan backwards from the closing date, and submit early. Should be practical, not just 'apply to everything'.

items.title: Reading a job advert
items.source: Civil Service Jobs adverts; Civil Service Success Profiles
items.body: A Civil Service advert is a guide to how you will be assessed, so read it all. The summary tells you about the team and the main duties. The person specification and essential criteria list what you must be able to show. Any desirable criteria are extra and helpful but not required. The advert says how you will be assessed, for example with a personal statement, a CV, behaviours, strengths, tests or an interview, and it gives the dates of each stage. Check also the salary, location, working pattern (full time, part time, flexible, hybrid), the security checks needed and any rules on nationality or residency. If you cannot meet an essential criterion you will normally be sifted out, so check this before you spend time on an application. The advert gives a contact for questions and for reasonable adjustments.

questions.prompt: Where in a Civil Service advert would you find how you will be assessed?

options.text: Only in the salary box
Nowhere, it is kept secret until the interview
Only in the department's annual report
In the sections on how to apply and the selection process

questions.prompt: An advert lists some criteria as essential. What does that mean?

options.text: You must be able to show them to be considered
They are only nice to have
Only people with a degree can show them
They are checked after you start

questions.prompt: An advert says interviews will take place in the week of 8 December and you are away that week. What should you do?

options.text: Apply anyway and say nothing
Contact the recruitment team before applying to see whether other dates are possible, or decide not to apply
Wait until you are offered an interview and then cancel it
Assume the dates will move to suit you

questions.prompt: An advert lists five essential criteria. You think you meet four, and for the fifth you have only a little evidence from voluntary work. Should you apply? What should you do?
questions.answer: Read the fifth criterion carefully and decide if it is a hard requirement (a qualification, right to work, a security rule) or a skill or experience you can show in different ways. If it is a hard requirement you cannot meet, do not apply. If it is a skill, apply and use your best evidence, including voluntary and unpaid experience, with specific examples and results. You can also contact the person named in the advert with questions. Be honest and do not overstate the evidence.
questions.rubric: Should separate hard requirements from skills, use voluntary experience as evidence, contact the named person with questions, and stay honest.

items.title: The stages from application to start date
items.source: Civil Service Recruitment Principles; Civil Service Jobs
items.body: The stages vary by department and by role but follow a pattern. First is the application, which may be a form, personal statement, CV or answers on behaviours. Next is the sift, where recruiters screen the applications against the criteria, and only those who meet the bar move on. Some roles then ask you to take online tests, for example verbal, numerical or situational judgement. Next comes an interview or assessment, often by video. If you are successful you receive a conditional offer, which depends on pre-employment checks such as identity, right to work, references and security clearance. Only when the checks are cleared do you get a start date. Do not resign from a current job or make firm plans until the checks are complete and you have a written confirmed start date.

options.text: The interview
The medical examination
The first screening of applications against the criteria
The final pay negotiation

questions.prompt: Which is the usual order of stages?

options.text: Interview, application, start date, checks, offer
Offer, application, sift, interview, checks
Checks, offer, application, interview, start date
Application, sift, tests or interview, conditional offer, checks, start date

questions.prompt: What does a conditional offer mean?

options.text: The job is yours only if the pre-employment checks are cleared
You may start work the next day
The offer will be withdrawn if you ask about pay
You have to pass another interview first

questions.prompt: You receive a conditional offer. What should you do and what should you avoid?
questions.answer: Accept it in writing by the deadline given, and complete the checks promptly: send identity and right to work documents, give accurate employment and address history, and return any forms. Keep the recruitment team up to date and answer queries fast. Avoid giving notice at a current job, signing a lease or committing to childcare costs until all checks are cleared and you have a confirmed start date in writing, because the offer can be withdrawn if checks fail or take time.
questions.rubric: Should say to accept, complete checks quickly with accurate information, and avoid resigning or committing money until confirmed in writing.

items.title: Fair recruitment, Disability Confident and adjustments
items.source: Civil Service Commission, Recruitment Principles; Disability Confident scheme
items.body: Civil Service jobs are filled on merit through fair and open competition, as set out in the Recruitment Principles that the independent Civil Service Commission oversees. On merit means the person who best meets the criteria gets the job, regardless of background. Departments take part in the Disability Confident scheme: a disabled applicant who meets the minimum criteria for the role is offered an interview. Applicants can ask for reasonable adjustments at any stage, for example extra time in a test, a different format or a more accessible interview. Ask as early as you can, using the contact in the advert, and describe what would help. Asking for an adjustment does not count against you. Many roles also offer part-time, job-share and flexible working, which suits people with caring responsibilities.

questions.prompt: What does it mean that Civil Service jobs are filled on merit?

options.text: The person with the most years of service is chosen
The person who best meets the criteria after fair and open competition is chosen
The person recommended by a minister is chosen
The first applicant is chosen

questions.prompt: Under the Disability Confident scheme, what is offered to a disabled applicant who meets the minimum criteria for the role?

options.text: An automatic job
A higher salary
An interview
Exemption from checks

questions.prompt: You have dyslexia and a test has a strict time limit. What is the best step?

options.text: Say nothing and hope for the best
Skip the test
Tell them only after you have failed
Contact the recruitment team as early as possible to request a reasonable adjustment such as extra time

questions.prompt: You are worried that having been out of work for years will count against you. What would you say and do?
questions.answer: Recruitment is on merit against the criteria, so a career break is not a reason to be turned down. Be honest about the break in one short sentence, then focus on evidence: specific examples of planning, organising, communicating, budgeting, caring or voluntary work that show the skills asked for. Look out for roles that welcome flexible working or those who are returning to work, and use the contact in the advert to ask about support. Prepare and practise to build confidence.
questions.rubric: Should say merit-based, honest about the gap, focus on skills evidence from unpaid work, and ask for support. Should not recommend hiding the gap.
